reference: Documented caps file/no-xattr and pure name-validation contracts with private files. Bash metadata remains separate. Populated xattr decoding and process capability operations need fixed UAPI bytes with reviewed syscall/xattr mocks; no matching GNU CLI parity is claimed.
coverage: Bash type metadata identifies caps as a builtin.
Bash help metadata advertises the documented probe, drop, add, clear, file, and has verbs.
Deferred: capability set inspection and -V bindings against independent kernel mask observations.
Deferred: capability name lookup and effective-set membership across low and high capability indices.
Deferred: add/drop/clear state transitions and capset/prctl permission failures in disposable children or syscall mocks.
Deferred: one-way bounding-set changes and clear all ordering in fresh disposable processes or mocks.
Deferred: security.capability xattr decoding against fixed vfs_cap_data bytes and getxattr outcomes.
Deferred: malformed arguments and kernel error paths with syscall-call recording.
Actual private-file no-capability and missing-file results, empty variable binding and pure unknown-name rejection.
exclusions: Process capability probes/mutations and populated security.capability decoding remain deferred to fixed-state VM/syscall/xattr mocks. Private files created here are read without changing capability state.
No setuid/file-capability executable, installed identity, host xattr, or host capability state is inspected.
No direct GNU parity claim: capsh/setpriv do not implement the same CLI contract.

cases.purpose: Check availability through Bash's type builtin without invoking caps operations.
Check the documented Bash help metadata lists each advertised caps verb; the script only reads help output.
cases.script:
help caps > help.txt
h=$(<help.txt)
for word in 'caps probe [-V VAR]' 'caps drop SET CAP1,CAP2,...' 'caps add SET CAP1,CAP2,...' 'caps clear SET' 'caps file PATH [-V VAR]' 'caps has CAP'; do
  [[ $h == *"$word"* ]] || exit 1
done
printf 'probe drop add clear file has\n'
cases.stdout: probe drop add clear file has

cases.purpose: Validate the five rendered capability sets and -V bindings using fixed, independently known masks.
Check positive and negative effective-set membership, case-insensitive names, optional CAP_ prefix, and a capability index above bit 31.
Check drop/add behavior across permitted, effective, inheritable, and ambient sets, including kernel-rejected raises.
Check clear for individual sets and the ordering and final state of clear all, including the one-way bounding set.
Check security.capability revision 2 and 3 decoding, effective flag handling, empty xattrs, malformed payload lengths, and -V binding.
cases.reason: Remaining obligations: r6: Only lengths 0, 4, 11, 12, 16 and 19 were observed; the two full malformed-length ranges were not exhaustively exercised.

cases.purpose: Check missing operands, unknown verbs/sets/capability names, and accepted case/prefix variants with exact status and diagnostics.
Check errno propagation and partial-operation behavior when capability syscalls fail at selected points.
Read only the newly created private file; absent or unsupported security.capability yields the documented empty result and variable binding.
cases.script:
: > ordinary
caps file ordinary
value=sentinel
caps file ordinary -V value
printf 'value=%s\n' "$value"

cases.purpose: A missing private file returns an xattr read failure without inspecting process capabilities.
Reject an unknown capability name in the pure lookup path before capget.
